title: Energy & Chemicals
meta: Operational excellence for Canadian energy and chemical operators: KPIs, Lean process improvement and change management that your plant teams own and sustain.
h1: Safer, leaner plant operations your teams own and sustain
lead: We help energy and chemical operators find hidden capacity, cut non-value-added work and build KPIs that connect the control room to the boardroom. Your people drive the change, so the gains last after we leave.
intro: Where does performance slip in a process plant?

In energy and chemicals, margin is won or lost in the details: unplanned downtime, slow turnarounds, maintenance backlogs, manual reporting and procedures that drift from how work is really done. Chmltech is led by a process engineer, so we understand unit operations, management of change and process safety as well as Lean and Six Sigma. We map how work actually flows, measure it against clear KPIs and work alongside your operators, engineers and supervisors to remove waste. The result is a culture of continuous improvement that keeps paying dividends long after the project ends.
signs: Turnarounds regularly run over schedule or budget
The maintenance backlog keeps growing despite overtime
MOC and permit paperwork slows routine work to a crawl
Shift reports and KPIs are compiled by hand in spreadsheets
Operators and management see different numbers for the same unit
challenges: Reactive maintenance and poor work planning take units offline and erode throughput. Without reliable data it is hard to see which failures matter most.
Scope creep, late materials and weak sequencing stretch turnarounds and push costs well past plan.
PSM, MOC and regulatory reporting are essential, but manual, paper-heavy workflows consume engineering time and invite errors.
Frontline teams, engineering and executives often track different metrics, so improvement efforts pull in different directions.
services: We define key metrics for service levels, productivity, speed and quality across your critical processes, set the baseline and use them to measure the success of each change.
A thorough as-is analysis: process mapping, financial and operating data review, direct observation in the field and a map of the management tools you use today.
Structured observations separate value-added from non-value-added activity, revealing capacity hidden in maintenance, logistics, lab and administrative workflows.
We help tighten work scoping, sequencing and backlog management so planned work gets done and shutdowns run closer to schedule.
We assess change readiness up front and build a plan so your own people lead the change and keep ownership of their improved processes.
We work with your leadership to translate strategy into daily activities everyone understands, and automate reporting and approvals where it adds value.

steps.label: Notification raised
steps.text: An operator or inspector reports a defect on equipment in the unit.

steps.label: Planning and scoping
steps.text: A planner scopes the job, estimates labour and identifies parts, permits and isolations.

steps.label: Parts and permits
steps.text: Materials are staged and work permits, isolations and any MOC reviews are completed.

steps.label: Scheduled execution
steps.text: Crews complete the job in a scheduled window with the unit prepared for safe work.

steps.label: Close-out
steps.text: History, failure codes and lessons learned are recorded so reliability data improves.

config.fix_text: Standard job plans, clear priority rules and a weekly scheduling meeting let planners keep ahead of incoming work instead of firefighting.

layers.label: Safe, stable operations
layers.text: Process safety, PSM and MOC discipline come first; every improvement must protect them.

layers.label: Agreed KPIs and baseline
layers.text: Shared measures for service, productivity, speed and quality, with a baseline everyone trusts.

layers.label: Standard work
layers.text: Clear procedures and job plans that reflect how the work is actually done in the field.

layers.label: Daily management
layers.text: Short shift huddles and visual boards that surface problems early and assign owners.

layers.label: Team-led improvement
layers.text: Operators and technicians identify and solve problems themselves, supported by leadership.

examples: Planned shutdown of a process unit
Scope was finalized late and contractors waited on materials, stretching the shutdown past plan.
Scope freeze dates, staged materials and a sequenced schedule keep the work on a tighter, more predictable timeline.
Routine MOCs circulated on paper for weeks, waiting for signatures from busy engineers.
A risk-tiered digital MOC workflow routes simple changes quickly and reserves full review for higher-risk items.
A shift supervisor spent the first hour of each shift copying historian data into a spreadsheet.
An automated daily report and a short huddle board free that time for walking the unit and solving problems.
outcomes: Clear KPIs linking frontline work to business results
More planned and fewer reactive maintenance jobs
Shorter, more predictable turnarounds and shutdowns
Leaner MOC, permit and reporting workflows without weakening safety
Teams that own and sustain their improved processes

faq: Will process improvement compromise process safety or MOC?

No. Safety and PSM requirements are the foundation of every change we propose. Where we streamline MOC or permit workflows, we keep the required reviews and make the low-risk path faster rather than removing controls.
Can you help before or during a turnaround?
Yes. We can review scope, planning and sequencing ahead of a turnaround, and help you capture lessons learned afterwards so the next one runs better.
Do you work with smaller operators and chemical producers?
Yes. Much of our work is with Canadian SMEs, including specialty chemical producers, energy service companies and smaller facilities that need practical improvement without a large consulting team.
We agree KPIs and a baseline at the start, covering service levels, productivity, speed and quality. Progress is tracked against those measures and an agreed ROI target throughout the engagement.
